text.p: North Face Inc said Wednesday its chief financial officer, Roxanna Prahser, had resigned in order to spend more time with her family.
William Simon, president and chief executive of the outerwear company, said North Face had hired a search firm and was currently interviewing candidates to succeed Prahser.
The company also said it had won a subcontract to design and develop a new type of backpack and load system for the Army that would be part of a modular body armor and modular backpack system.

The initial phase of the contract is for 18 months. The pact includes options for the production of more than 100,000 units over the next seven years; if all production options were exercised, maximum revenues would be $20 million between 1999 and 2003, the company said.
North Face went public last year, opening at about $19 on its first day of trading. It closed Tuesday at 22-3/4.
